desktop_software.name: WinMax Desktop
desktop_software.description: Exact replica of machine control software for PC use

conversational_programming.description: Hurco's proprietary programming method where the operator fills in fields in a guided interface rather than writing G-code line by line
program_creation_workflow: Create new conversational program (auto-named 'no-name' + sequential number)
Optional: Save As to specific location
Set up tools in Tool Setup

position_blocks.typical_use: End of program to present part to operator for change/flip

lines_and_arcs.programming_model: Sequential segments building a contour from start to end point

pattern_blocks.description: Repeat previously programmed operations in patterns (linear, bolt circle, etc.)

nc_program_call.description: Merge conversational program with NC (G-code) program
nc_program_call.use_case: Combine conversational ease with CAM-generated G-code for complex operations

field_help.description: Bottom-left corner of screen shows context help for highlighted field
field_help.graphics_assist: Advanced tool settings show graphical indication of what each field represents

helix_plunge.location: Program Parameters > Milling tab > Plunge Type
helix_plunge.purpose: Controls how tool enters a pocket (ramping into material)
helix_plunge.use_case: Non-center-cutting endmills that cannot straight plunge

helix_geometry.location: Milling > Lines and Arcs > Helix segment type
helix_geometry.purpose: Create finished-to-size geometry using helical interpolation (simultaneous XYZ motion)
use_cases: Helical boring to open holes to exact size
helix_geometry.motion_type: Constant 3-axis XYZ ramping motion along circular path

helix_bore_workflow: Start in Lines and Arcs block
Set XY start point (on the contour of desired hole)
Calculate from diameter: X_start = diameter/2 from center
Set Z start above material (critical: do NOT put Z bottom here)
Set direction (CW or CCW for climb/conventional)
Leave X/Y end points BLANK (let math assist calculate)
Set Z end point (final depth of hole)
Use cutter compensation (left comp for climb cut inside hole)

critical_tips.z_bottom_mistake: Most common error: putting overall Z depth in first segment Z bottom field. Keep Z bottom ABOVE material for the starting segment, then use helix Z-end for actual depth.
critical_tips.xy_end_blank: Do NOT enter X/Y end points in helix segment. Leave blank and let WinMax math assist calculate the endpoint automatically.
critical_tips.pre_drill: Usually drill center of hole first, then helix bore to final size — not required but common practice
critical_tips.cutter_comp: Use left cutter comp for climb cutting around inside of circle (counterclockwise)

thread_milling.description: Uses same helical motion as helix bore but follows thread geometry
thread_milling.relationship_to_helix: Both use simultaneous XYZ constant motion (helical interpolation)
thread_milling.programming_location: Milling > Lines and Arcs > Thread Mill segment type
thread_milling.tool_motion: Helical interpolation around thread centerline with Z advancement per revolution equal to thread pitch

adaptipath.software_option: Part of UltiPockets option on Hurco machines
adaptipath.description: Hurco's adaptive/trochoidal milling strategy — constant tool engagement pocketing
adaptipath.principle: Maintains constant width of cut (radial engagement) throughout the entire toolpath, eliminating the engagement spikes that occur during step-over transitions in conventional pocketing

cutting_strategy.approach: Large depth of cut with small width of cut (radial step-over)
cutting_strategy.depth: Use full flute length if needed
cutting_strategy.type: Roughing strategy — typically followed by finish pass

circular_pockets.description: Spiral outward from center maintaining constant step-over
circular_pockets.sound: Entire cut sounds the same — no variation in cutting sound
circular_pockets.guarantee: Will never exceed specified width of cut

non_circular_geometry.description: Control finds optimal start location for maximum spiral, then transitions to zigzag or one-way when spiral cannot be maintained

zigzag.description: When spiral can no longer maintain step-over, cuts back and forth (alternating climb and conventional)
zigzag.behavior: Never exceeds specified width of cut even during transitions

one_way.description: Takes a climb cut, lifts slightly in Z for transition, repositions, takes another climb cut
one_way.benefit: Always climb cutting — preferred by most users
one_way.transition_move: Arc move to transition, slight Z lift to prevent dragging across part

toolpath_behavior.with_islands: Control adapts spiral and transition moves to work around islands while maintaining constant engagement

speed_feed_guidance.principle: Dial in feeds and speeds on a straight-line side cut at full depth. Those same parameters work for pocketing because AdaptiPath guarantees tool never engages more material than that straight cut.
speed_feed_guidance.feed_rate: Significantly higher than conventional pocketing — limited only by side-cut conditions

programming_in_winmax.location: Milling > Frame or Lines and Arcs pocket block
programming_in_winmax.activation: Enable AdaptiPath option in pocket parameters

tool_library.description: Library of all tools ever set up on the machine

input_options.option_1: Surface footage + Chip load per flute + Number of flutes → Control calculates RPM and IPM
input_options.option_2: Direct RPM + Direct feed rate (IPM) → Control calculates SFM and chip load

speed_feed_data.auto_populate: When tool is called in a program, pre-configured speeds/feeds auto-fill program fields

visual_feedback.advanced_tool_settings: Shows graphic of tool with highlighted dimension as user moves through fields
visual_feedback.color_assignment: Sequential color per tool in graphics, or user can force specific colors (useful for engraving contrast)

stock_geometry.auto_sizing: Control automatically creates stock slightly larger than programmed geometry if no manual sizing

manual_sizing.reference_position: Default front-left corner at zero; can be changed to center, back-left, etc.

part_setup.program_from: All coordinates are relative to the chosen work zero position

program_manager.description: Central screen for creating, opening, and saving programs
program_manager.disk_operations: Windows Explorer-style file tree for cut/copy/paste/create directories
program_manager.active_programs: Shows currently open programs (running or in preparation)

file_management.save_optional: Programs can be written and run without saving (useful for one-off fixtures)

workflow: Turn on main power switch (breaker, then machine switch on back)
Wait for Windows-based control to boot (several minutes)
Press Cycle Start to enable servo drives
Press Calibrate Machine button (homes all axes — Z up, X/Y to back corner)
Press Cycle Start again to calibrate tool magazine
Run built-in warm-up cycle (steps through RPMs up to max, e.g., 12,000 RPM)
Optionally turn on coolant during warm-up to cycle and aerate

calibration_detail.axes_calibration: Z goes up first, then X/Y move to back corner (homing sequence)
calibration_detail.tool_changer_calibration: Separate step after axis calibration — prompted by control

warm_up_cycle.description: Machine runs back and forth stepping through RPM increments to full speed
warm_up_cycle.best_practice: Run coolant during warm-up for thermal conditioning

workflow: Call up probe tool (T99) via Tool Management
Jog to approximate center/top of workpiece
Select probing routine (rectangular probe for rectangular stock)
Set zero position type (XY center + Z top is common)
Execute probe cycle — auto-measures and sets work coordinates
probing_and_work_offsets.manual_tool_call: In Manual mode: go to Tool Management, type tool number on keypad, press Enter, then Cycle Start
probing_and_work_offsets.enter_key_importance: On Hurco controls, you MUST press Enter for any typed value to be applied — critical operational note
probing_and_work_offsets.jog_control: Use jog wheel (handwheel) on pendant for manual axis movement

mt_connect.configuration: Accessible through Windows system menus on the control
mt_connect.note: Can be enabled for machine monitoring and data collection

graphics_and_simulation.solid_model_graphics: WinMax builds a solid model of the part being cut, showing stock removal in real time
graphics_and_simulation.verification: Run program graphically to verify toolpaths before cutting
graphics_and_simulation.tool_accuracy: More accurate tool geometry descriptions (drill point angle, etc.) produce more accurate graphic previews
graphics_and_simulation.color_coding: Each tool assigned different color for visual distinction in graphics

key_additions: Improved graphics and solid model simulation

specifications.axes: 5-axis (3 linear + 2 rotary via swiveling rotary table)

spindle_speed_range.note: High-speed spindle for small diameter cutters and fine finishing

key_capabilities.complex_part_production: Swiveling rotary table enables complex parts with fewer setups
key_capabilities.precision: Exceptional accuracy from rigid construction and thermal stability

high_feed_milling_on_dmu60.description: HFM (High Feed Milling) is a key strategy on the DMU 60 eVo
high_feed_milling_on_dmu60.principle: Specialized tooling with small lead angles enables higher feed rates while minimizing radial cutting forces
benefits: Increased productivity through higher feed rates
Reduced mechanical stress on machine components
Extended tool life by distributing wear across larger cutting edge portion

setup_requirements.workholding: High rigidity solutions — hydraulic fixtures or zero-point clamping systems
setup_requirements.tool_holders: Hydraulic chucks or shrink-fit holders for minimal runout and maximum rigidity
setup_requirements.runout_requirement: Critical to minimize tool runout for HFM success

cam_programming.strategy: Adaptive toolpaths ensuring consistent cutting engagement

tool_selection.roughing: Indexable high-feed cutters with replaceable inserts
tool_selection.finishing: Solid carbide endmills with high-feed geometries

titanium.depth_of_cut: Shallow, with focus on chip evacuation

tribal_knowledge_tips.tip: When programming a helix bore in WinMax Lines & Arcs, set the first segment Z-bottom ABOVE the material surface. The actual Z depth goes in the helix segment Z-end field. Most common mistake is putting overall depth in the start segment.
In WinMax helix programming, leave X/Y end point fields BLANK. The control's math assist will calculate the correct endpoint. Entering values manually often causes errors.
On Hurco controls, you MUST press Enter for any typed value to be applied. Simply typing a number is not enough — it will not register until Enter is pressed.
Hurco calibration is two steps: first axes home (Z up, XY to back corner), then tool magazine calibrates separately. Both require Cycle Start press. Takes about 30 seconds total.
During warm-up cycle, also turn on coolant to let it cycle and aerate. This helps with thermal conditioning and ensures coolant system is primed before cutting.

Set speeds and feeds in Tool Setup before programming. When a tool is called in a conversational program, the control auto-populates speed/feed fields from the tool setup, saving time and reducing errors.
WinMax speed/feed fields are bidirectional: enter SFM + chip load and it calculates RPM + IPM, OR enter RPM + IPM and it calculates SFM + chip load. Use whichever format your tooling data provides.

For AdaptiPath parameters: dial in your feeds and speeds on a straight-line side cut at full depth of cut first. Those exact parameters will work for pocketing because AdaptiPath guarantees the tool never engages more material than a straight side cut.
AdaptiPath one-way mode is preferred over zigzag for most applications. It always climb cuts with a slight Z-lift transition between passes, preventing tool drag across the part surface.
NEVER use compressed air to blow chips on a DMG MORI lathe. Air pushes chips under way covers and into bedways, causing accelerated wear. Always use coolant hose or wash-down pump instead.

Old machinist trick for boring bar chatter: keep back set screws tight but back off the front screw, then slowly snug it while listening to the cut. The front screw acts as a vibration tuner — the pressure dampens bar harmonics. Adjust by feel/sound until chatter disappears.
DMG MORI lathes use 32 hydraulic oil for the hydraulic system (chuck actuation, tailstock, etc.). Check level at reservoir on rear of machine during daily maintenance.
Parts catcher has replaceable liners: Teflon for standard work, copper liner available for specialty metals. Position is adjustable via set screw and is programmable from the control.
For High Feed Milling on the DMU 60 eVo, use hydraulic fixtures or zero-point clamping systems. Standard vise clamping may not provide sufficient rigidity for the extreme feed rates used in HFM.
Use hydraulic chucks or shrink-fit holders for HFM operations on the DMU 60 eVo. Minimal tool runout is critical for high-feed cutting success and tool life.
